chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who dies leaving a slave mother and wealth, that his mother is purchased from his wealth and the remainder of the wealth is given to her if there is no relative of his who has a share in the Book (of inheritance).

Second: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Abu Thabit, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Isaac who said: A slave of Ali (peace be upon him) died, so he was asked if they could find an heir for him. It was said to him: Two daughters in Al-Yamamah who are slaves. So they purchased them from the deceased's wealth and then gave them the remainder of the wealth.

Third: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafsh, from Abdillah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who died leaving much wealth and a slave mother and a slave sister. He said: They are purchased from the deceased's wealth, then freed and inherit. I said: What if the owners of the girl refuse? He said: It is not for them to refuse; they are valued at a fair price and their money is given according to the valuation. I said: If they were purchased, then freed, then inherited, who would inherit them? He said: The manumitters of their son would inherit them because they were purchased from the son's wealth.

Fourth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to rule regarding a free man who dies leaving a slave mother, that she is purchased from his son's wealth, then freed and she is inherited.

Fifth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdillah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say regarding a man who died leaving wealth and a slave mother: His mother is purchased and freed, and then the remainder of the wealth is given to her.

Sixth: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man dies leaving a slave son. He said: He is purchased and freed, and then what remains is given to him.

Seventh: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man dies leaving his father who is a slave or his mother who is a slave, and the deceased is free, his father or relative is purchased from what he left, and the remainder of the wealth is inherited.

Eighth: Ali ibn Al-Hasan from Muhammad and Ahmad, sons of Al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man dies leaving his father who is a slave or his mother who is a slave or his brother or sister, and he left wealth and the deceased is free, he is purchased from what his father or relative left, and the remainder of the wealth is inherited.

Ninth: As for what Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Abu Thabit and Ibn Awn, from Al-Sa'i, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say regarding a man who died leaving wealth and a slave mother: She is purchased and freed, and then his wealth is given to her if he has no agnates (asabah). If he has agnates, the wealth is divided between her and the agnates. This report is not acted upon by consensus of the Righteous Sect, because with the existence of agnates, if they are free, it is not obligatory to purchase the mother, but rather the inheritance belongs to them. And it is only obligatory to purchase her if there is no one among the free who inherits, whether near or far. And whenever the mother becomes free, the inheritance is hers alone without the agnates with us, without disagreement. So the report is set aside with us in all cases, unless we carry it on a type of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) when the freedom of the mother is established, because the general public (Sunni) give her one-third and give the remainder to the agnates. And that which indicates what we considered is that one of those mentioned should only be purchased if there is no heir there.

Tenth: What Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Bakkar, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who died leaving a slave son and left no heir other than him, and left wealth: He said: The son is purchased and freed, and the remainder of the wealth is inherited by him.

Eleventh: And as for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Abdillah and Ja'far and Muhammad ibn Abbas, from Ula, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them, who said: The free and the slave do not inherit from each other.
Twelfth: From him, he said: Abdillah ibn Jabalah narrated to them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free and the slave do not inherit from each other.

Thirteenth: From him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to them from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free and the slave do not inherit from each other. The meaning in these reports is that the free and the slave do not inherit from each other in that each inherits the other, because the slave owns nothing so it is valid that he is inherited, and he does not inherit the free man unless there is no one else. As for with the existence of others among the free, there is no mutual inheritance between them in any case.

Fourteenth: And as for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from Jamil, from Fadil ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The slave does not inherit and the freedman does not inherit. The meaning in this report is that the slave does not inherit with the existence of a free person there. As for with the absence of one, then he inherits him according to what we presented. And that which indicates that with the existence of a free heir, even if he is further away than the slave, it is not obligatory to purchase the slave.

Fifteenth: What Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Mizham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a Muslim slave who has a Christian mother, and the slave has a free son: It was said: What do you think if the slave's mother died and left wealth? He said: Her free grandson inherits her.

Sixteenth: And Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated, saying: Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed a man died leaving a brother who was a slave and bequeathed to him one thousand dirhams. So his master refused to validate it for him, so they appealed to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. He said to the boy: Do you have children? He said: Yes. He said: Are they free? He said: Yes. He said: So do you accept from all the wealth one thousand dirhams while they inherit your uncle? Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was correct.

Seventeenth: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when a man died leaving a slave wife, would purchase her from his wealth, free her, and then inherit her. The meaning in this report is that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) acted in the manner of voluntary giving, because we have clarified that if the wife is free and there is no heir, she does not have more than one-fourth, and the remainder belongs to the Imam. And if the one entitled to the wealth is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), it is permissible for him to purchase the wife, free her, and give her the remainder of the wealth as a voluntary gift and recommendation, without that action being obligatory and binding.

key_terms.عَصَبَةٌ: Agnates (male relatives who inherit by residue)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on purchasing a deceased's slave parent or child from their estate to grant them inheritance?
ai.summary: This collection from Al-Istibsar elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'shira' al-am' (purchasing the slave) to ensure the emancipation and inheritance of a deceased's slave parent or child, a practice rooted in Imam Ali’s rulings. The text critically reconciles apparent contradictions regarding mutual inheritance between free and slave individuals by distinguishing between scenarios with and without other free heirs, while also addressing the status of agnates (asabah) and the voluntary nature of certain emancipation acts by the Imam.
